newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gunman kills one in failed Swiss bank holdup.
newsitem.headline: Gunman kills one in failed Swiss bank holdup.

text.p: A gunman killed a Swiss bank employee and took two hostages on Wednesday but was overpowered by police as he tried to make off with a ransom payment, police said.
The armed man entered Regio Bank in Lucerne in central Switzerland in the early morning and shot one member of staff, wounding him so badly he later died of his wounds, a police spokesman said.

The 49-year-old gunman, a local resident with a police record, then holed up in an upstairs office with two hostages -- a man and a woman who both worked at the bank -- and demanded a million Swiss francs ($700,000) ransom.

Security forces in the picturesque town much visited by tourists cordoned off the bank building and positioned snipers on neighbouring rooftops as police spoke with the gunman by internal telephone line, via the hostages.
"He wanted to leave the house with the hostages," the spokesman said. "The money was prepared, but not a million. It was less," he added.

After sending the woman out to collect the money, the gunman demanded a getaway car in what police suspected was a bid to distract their attention. He then tried to leave the building with the male hostage.
The hostage was able to maintain a slight distance from the gunman, so police closed in and overpowered the man without having to fire a shot, the spokesman said.
A Reuter photographer at the scene said police led the man away in his underwear and with a bag over his head.
